labelledFrom: VAmPI source code in the erev0s/vampi:latest image (api_views/*.py, models/*.py), read on 2026-11-20
scope: Access-control categories only. Out of scope: SQL injection (GET /users/v1/{username}), mass assignment of admin=true at registration (OWASP API3), user/password enumeration, ReDoS, unauthenticated user listing (GET /users/v1 is public by design).
unit: One case = (HTTP method, OpenAPI path template, category).

cases.source: api_views/books.py:get_by_title
cases.notes: vulnerable=1 looks the book up by title only; returns secret and owner (username) of any user. vulnerable=0 filters by the caller.

cases.source: api_views/users.py:update_password
cases.notes: vulnerable=1 changes the password of the user in the path. vulnerable=0 changes the caller's own password but still answers 204 (true negative with 2xx). No read-back endpoint exists, so the effect is not observable through the API.

cases.source: api_views/users.py:update_email
cases.notes: Both modes update the CALLER's e-mail (token sub) and ignore the path username; returns 204. True negative with 2xx.

cases.source: api_views/users.py:delete_user
cases.notes: Admin check enforced in both modes (non-admins get 401).

cases.source: api_views/users.py:debug
cases.notes: Debug function returns all users with passwords and admin flags without authentication, in BOTH modes ("bad practice" kept by VAmPI). Intended policy (admin-only) is not in the VAmPI spec and must be supplied by configuration.
